cases.name: Jackie Jo Torrez
cases.about:
(She)worked as a clinical therapist and social media coordinator for McDowell Healing Arts Center, 3253 Congress Ave., and had a master’s degree in social work.

She’d been a licensed social worker since August 2020. Her biography on the center’s website states she specialized in children, domestic violence, trauma, and post-traumatic stress disorder.

“Word can’t describe what she and her daughter mean to us,” said Dr. Melvin C. McDowell Jr., the agency’s founder and Torrez’s boss and mentor. Torrez had worked for McDowell for five years and been a student and intern of his.

He recalled holding Torrez’s daughter for the first time.

It meant the world to him when Torrez referred to him as “Uncle Mel.”

“It breaks my/our hearts that she left this world in the manner in which she did,” McDowell said. “She didn’t deserve that. No human being deserves that.”

At the same time, McDowell is taking solace in remembering Torrez’s vivacious personality and commitment to helping others.

“It brings my heart joy to remember her contagious laugh, her huge heart, and her determination to help other women combat and work through domestic violence,” he said. “Jackie loved her job, she loved and advocated for her clients, and she will forever be loved and missed. MHAC won’t be the same without you, Jackie Jo.”
